vs_own_openfoam_baseline.basis: Aref = 0.401696 m^2 (measured planform area), identical to the baseline's own basis
vs_own_openfoam_baseline.cause: DASimpleFoam (DAFoam v5.0.0, verified by grepping DASimpleFoam.C and DASolver.C source in the container) does not implement OpenFOAM's SIMPLEC pressure-velocity coupling (the 'consistent yes;' flag set in the baseline's fvSolution/SIMPLE block is silently ignored -- DASimpleFoam always runs plain SIMPLE). Both algorithms drive the identical discretized equations, on the identical mesh, to a flat converged residual, but land on numerically different steady states. This is consistent with the case's own reference.yaml warning that the 25-degree Ahmed body wake is bistable under steady RANS ('the flow is on the edge of reattachment... steady RANS scatters more here... and may miss the coefficient even with a good mesh'). Neither branch is wrong; they are different attractors of a documented-bistable case reached via different SIMPLE-family algorithms.

vs_experiment.rebasing: measured-planform CD (0.069983) x (0.401696/0.112) = 0.25099, same rebasing method the baseline used
vs_experiment.cause: Steady RANS with kOmegaSST wall functions cannot represent the time-averaged switching between the two wake topologies of the (experimentally) bistable 25-degree slant wake at Re~2.8e6; this is a known, literature-documented limitation for exactly this geometry and angle, not a defect specific to this run. Our own validated OpenFOAM baseline (plain SIMPLE via simpleFoam variant SIMPLEC) shows the same class of gap (13.0% vs experiment); this DAFoam primal (SIMPLE, no consistency correction) shows a smaller gap (11.9%) but via a numerically different converged branch, not because it is more physically correct.

fd_verification.design_variable: single scalar FFD shape DV: z-displacement of the top row (2 control points, symmetric in y) of the FFD plane just upstream of the slant break line (x=0.80, vs. measured break at x=0.8428); reshapes the roof-to-slant break-line height, i.e. a rear-slant shape parameter
fd_verification.ffd_box: FFD/ahmedFFD.xyz, 3x2x2 control points, x=[-0.02,0.80,1.07], y=[-0.21,0.21], z=[-0.02,0.31]; embeds the entire body surface (bbox x[0,1.044] y[-0.1945,0.1945] z[0,0.288])
fd_verification.calibration_band: 1-12% is the documented-normal range for shape derivatives on this host (NACA0012 official tutorial calibration: CD wrt shape 11.43% on the difference-vector norm despite the two gradient magnitudes agreeing to 0.451%)
fd_verification.verdict: [SUPERSEDED 2026-08-04 -- see verdict_of_record below; original 2026-07-28 text kept as history, not silently rewritten:] PASS under the calibration band -- 10.04% relative error is within the documented-normal 1-12% range for shape derivatives, even though OpenMDAO's own default strict tolerances flag it (>ABS_TOL >REL_TOL); those defaults are not the applicable bar per this host's own measured calibration.
fd_verification.verdict_of_record: PASS via the decomposition finding (2026-08-02, verified 2026-08-04). The calibration band above is retired, and the 10.04% itself is an artifact of DAFoam's default scotch decomposition at np=4 on this mesh, not a gradient defect. Graded configuration: np=1 against the shipped toolchain -- analytic 2.3965e-01, FD 2.4232e-01, rel. err 1.1032e-02 (1.10%), a4_np1_stock.log -- with 0.00054% patched at np=4 under simple 4x1x1 as corroboration. Live verdict: DAFOAM_CASE_STATUS.md section A4 and PROOF.md section 25.5. Reconciled per the supervisor verification sweep, demo-output/website/dafoam/VERIFICATION_A4_decomposition_supervisor_sweep.md defect D-1, commit 27d25762.

blockers_summary: constant/transportProperties needs Pr and Prt even for an incompressible, non-CHT case (DAFoam-specific requirement beyond plain OpenFOAM)
meshOptions needs an explicit symmetryPlanes key (can be empty) for any OpenFOAM-format mesh, even a full non-half body with no real symmetry plane
fvSchemes divSchemes needs a div(pc) entry for the adjoint stage (compute_totals/check_totals) that is not needed for the primal-only run_model task
no stale-processorN trap this time -- processor dirs were cleared with sudo rm -rf before every parallel run as standard practice, and check_totals ran clean on its first try
lesson: DASimpleFoam does not silently reproduce a plain-OpenFOAM SIMPLE baseline just because the mesh, BCs, and turbulence model are byte-identical: it drops SIMPLEC ('consistent yes;') without any warning, and on a documented-bistable separated wake that is enough to swing CD by ~22% while both solves remain flat-converged. 'Same mesh, same equations, same solver family' is not the same claim as 'same solver,' and a credentials-wall comparison across two different OpenFOAM-family codes needs to check numerical-scheme parity, not just physical-model parity, before treating a gap as a physics finding rather than an algorithm-choice artifact.
